Scenario 7 — Retreat together, then turn and finish
Mage/Warrior/Priest (Team A) versus Mage/Hunter/Rogue (Team B)

THE CHALLENGE
Team A trails 17–19, with 20 points needed to win and five ticks remaining, from step 295 to 300. It needs three kills without conceding a death for SUCCESS. Use terminal Team A reward: +1 SUCCESS, 0 DRAW, −1 FAIL. A simultaneous threshold tie is a draw; a win on the final tick still counts. An ongoing zero reward is not a draw.

Team A starts with Mage at 21 HP, Warrior at 1 HP and Priest at 5 HP. Team B has Mage at 14 HP, Hunter at 20 HP and Rogue at 54 HP. HP means remaining health. The 20 × 10 battlefield contains 11 obstacles. Other configured classes begin dead and receive no decision in this four-tick winning sequence.

THE TEAM PROBLEM
An immediate kill is tempting, but protecting the next teammate action matters more. Warrior uses Charge to interrupt Rogue's coming threat, then retreats. Mage removes the already empowered enemy Mage before spending a turn preparing its own Burst. Priest's job changes with the danger: heal Warrior, then itself, then Mage twice. Those jobs fit together; neither damage greed nor always healing the smallest health bar describes the whole solution.

THE FEW RULES YOU NEED
A tick is one simultaneous decision. Each agent chooses movement plus a Basic attack/heal, an Ultimate special ability, or no combat. Ultimate replaces Basic; it is not a second attack. All actions are chosen from the same current information. Damage and healing resolve together, and an agent's already accepted attack still counts if it dies that tick. Moving away cannot dodge an attack already accepted now.

Warrior's Charge closes distance, damages and stuns the next decision. It does not erase this tick's accepted action. Rogue's close-range Ultimate becomes ready next tick; Hunter attacks from farther away. Priest's Basic heal reaches distance 3, subject to its own legal-action mask. Its large Ultimate is unavailable throughout this fight.

Mage's Burst spends a combat action preparing stronger later Basics. Here Burst on tick 2 first boosts damage on tick 3. Mage-B already starts empowered and attacks immediately. Nearby class auras modify damage, producing the fractional HP values below.

SharedObs shares current teammate sightings, not hidden opponents or their selected actions. Walls and pillars obstruct sight and attacks; bodies obstruct movement, not sight. Retreat moves away from danger; pursuit closes on a target. Directions are intentions: geometry and bodies determine actual positions and future attack or healing access.

THE OPPONENT
Select SharedObs and Reactive TDM ALPHA for Team B. The unchanged deterministic controller chooses fresh legal actions each tick, not a prerecorded response. Mage-B opens by attacking Mage-A; Hunter-B attacks Warrior-A, then Priest-A, then Mage-A as positions and health change. Rogue's Charge stun removes its tick-2 decision. This response sequence is an observed result of the rules and setup, not information Team A can read in advance.

ONE VERIFIED WINNING SEQUENCE
Every row is chosen together. Initially dead Team A slots Stay/no-combat. Tick-4 movements and Warrior's combat were completed as Stay/no-combat to make the author's example exact; they are not claimed to be the only valid choices.

Tick | Mage-A | Warrior-A | Priest-A
1 | Northeast; Basic Mage-B | North; Charge Rogue-B | Northeast; Basic-heal Warrior-A
2 | East; Burst | Northwest; Basic Rogue-B | East; Basic-heal self
3 | Northeast; Basic Rogue-B | West; no combat | Northeast; Basic-heal Mage-A
4 | Stay; Basic Hunter-B | Stay; no combat | Stay; Basic-heal Mage-A

WHY THE CHOICES WORK TOGETHER
Tick 1: Warrior passes up the tempting low-HP ranged targets and Charges Rogue, delaying the pursuer's next decision. Priest heals the 1-HP Warrior through Hunter's accepted attack, while both begin withdrawing. Mage kills Mage-B and moves Northeast, but still takes the enemy's already accepted empowered Basic: Mage survives at about 1.94 HP. The kill prevents another Mage-B attack next tick, not the one already committed.

Tick 2: Warrior damages the stunned Rogue while withdrawing Northwest; that damage prepares Mage's later finish. Mage spends this safer combat window on Burst and moves East toward Hunter. Priest moves East with Mage and heals itself through Hunter's attack, reaching about 7.90 HP. Mage is weaker, but self-healing is essential to keep the healer alive in this sequence.

Tick 3: Warrior continues West without attacking. Mage's empowered Basic kills Rogue while Mage and Priest move Northeast into the chase. Priest now heals Mage, which entered the tick at about 1.94 HP, while Hunter attacks it. Mage survives at about 4.84 HP. The healing target changes because the immediate threat changes.

Tick 4: Mage finishes Hunter, and Priest heals Mage again. Hunter's accepted final Basic still lands. The heal turns a simultaneous two-sided finish into a Team A win; Warrior stays out of the final exchange.

WHAT THIS SCENARIO IS DESIGNED TO TEST
- Teammate Modeling: prepare Rogue for a partner's finishing attack while relying on coordinated damage and healing during retreat.
- Opponent Modeling: account for Rogue's upcoming Ultimate and Hunter's changing legal damage targets.
- Crowd Control Prioritization: delay the immediate pursuer rather than simply disable the easiest kill.
- Basic Healing Target Prioritization: change recipients from Warrior to self to Mage, according to the next lethal threat.
- Basic Damage Target Prioritization: remove the empowered Mage, prepare and finish Rogue, then finish Hunter.
- Ultimate Damage Target Prioritization: spend Charge on the threat to the team's continued actions, not just on immediate kill value.
- Ultimate Timing (Burst): use a safe preparation window instead of activating whenever available.
- Tactical Obstacle Exploitation: account for obstacle-shaped routes and collision-adjusted positions while preserving future legal attack and healing access.
- Tactical Positioning (Retreat, Pursuit): let Warrior withdraw while Mage and Priest close together on the remaining enemies.
- Multi-Step Team-Level Planning: connect the protective opening, safe Burst window and successive supported finishes across four ticks.

RESULT, CAUSAL CHECKS AND LIMITS
Scores after the four ticks are 18–19, 18–19, 19–19 and 20–19. Team A wins at step 299, before the time limit, with reward +1: terminated is true and truncated is false. No Team A agent dies. Final Mage/Warrior/Priest HP is approximately 6.84/3.90/7.90. All submitted actions are legal and accepted unchanged; repeating the same start and actions reproduces the trajectory.

Four original r25 checks, repeated on this setup, make the healing dependence concrete. With every other choice held fixed, omit the opening Warrior heal and Warrior dies on tick 1; omit the tick-2 self-heal and Priest dies on tick 2; omit the tick-3 Mage heal and Mage dies alongside Rogue on tick 3. Each loses. Omit only the final Mage heal and Mage dies alongside Hunter, producing a 20–20 DRAW. These checks test this continuation, not every possible substitute plan.
